sources.title: 2025 Resilience Report: Climate, Conflict and Resilience: Pathways to Sustainable and Inclusive Solutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Mali case study in a nine-country FCAS resilience report published in May 2025; field and referenced evidence span different dates.
sources.methodology: Triangulated quantitative data, desk review and key-informant field research across nine case studies.
sources.limitations: Fragile-context data gaps and attribution difficulty limit generalizability; informal coping may be missed.

sources.title: Addressing climate and conflict-related loss and damage in fragile states: a focus on Mali
sources.organization: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED), with DanChurchAid Mali and TASSAGHT
sources.temporal_coverage: Household research in five Mopti communes; hazard, mobility and loss findings cover differing retrospective periods, including the latest disaster year reported by sampled households.
sources.methodology: Household survey, focus groups and key-informant interviews in five Mopti communes; 408 households, 22 focus groups and four key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: The displaced-household sample was smaller because access, time and resources constrained recruitment; regression shows association, not causation.

sources.title: Practical solutions at the intersection of climate action, peace, and security in the Liptako-Gourma region
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), West and Central Africa Regional Hub / Liptako-Gourma Stabilization Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional study with interviews and field research conducted in 2024; the UNDP publication page dates release to 16 September 2025.
sources.methodology: Literature review, environmental and conflict-data analysis, key-informant interviews, case studies and field observations where possible.
sources.limitations: Conflict restricted engagement; the sample may favor accessible and secure areas; interviews and case studies may be subjective and findings may not generalize beyond the region.

sources.title: Mali, Decentralized evaluation of the Integrated Resilience Package in 20 priority communes (2018–2024)
sources.organization: World Food Programme (WFP), Mali Country Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Evaluation concerns the Integrated Resilience Package implemented from 2018 to 2024; WFP page published 7 January 2026.
sources.methodology: WFP Mali commissioned a qualitative and quantitative evaluation with stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Only the official portal synopsis was accessible; detailed methods, commune names and disaggregated results were not reviewed.

sources.title: Building peace and prosperity through climate action in Mali
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP programme story published 27 August 2025; examples and testimony are presented as programme and community accounts at that time.
sources.methodology: UNDP programme story with resident testimony and activity descriptions.
sources.limitations: Programme and self-reported examples; not representative or independently evaluated.

claims.locator: Printed pp.37–38, Environment and Natural Disasters
claims.paraphrase: Northern Mali faces drought and extreme heat with stressed reserves; southern river deltas face flooding where agriculture is clustered.
claims.limitations: Broad north/south zones in a 2025 synthesis.

claims.locator: Printed p.37, farmer-herder conflict and Liptako-Gourma; endnote 127
claims.paraphrase: In Liptako-Gourma, floods and droughts compound smallholder losses alongside land-ownership tensions and declining security.
claims.limitations: The report rejects climate change as the root cause of farmer-herder conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Variability and degradation may indirectly affect pre-existing farmer-herder conflict.

claims.locator: Printed pp.38–39, livelihood constraints and coping
claims.paraphrase: Conflict risks and tensions can prevent some people from moving toward better prospects, leaving tree-cutting or overgrazing as fallback livelihoods.
claims.limitations: Some cases only; prevalence is not quantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Conflict risk constrains mobility and may force degrading fallback livelihoods.

claims.paraphrase: Reported adaptations include pastoral herd-splitting and purchased feed, drought-tolerant crops, zaï pits, stone bunds and composting.
claims.limitations: Reported practices, not prevalence or scaled effectiveness.

claims.locator: PDF p.20, Kouna village, Sio commune focus-group example
claims.paraphrase: Kouna village in Sio commune, beside a pond fed by runoff and Niger levels, reportedly floods annually up to its streets.
claims.limitations: A translated focus-group account, not an instrument-based flood-frequency series.

claims.locator: PDF p.8, summary regression results on climate risk, conflict exposure and displacement
claims.paraphrase: In the Mopti sample, fewer climate risks correlated with lower mobility; lower violence and insecurity correlated with threefold lower displacement likelihood.
claims.limitations: Observational regression in 408 households; associations do not establish causal effects or representative regional rates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors treat climate risks and conflict exposure as distinct factors associated with migration or forced displacement.

claims.locator: PDF p.9, loss-and-damage summary by household migration status
claims.paraphrase: Among sampled displaced households, drought losses equalled 61% and flood losses 40% of annual income, versus 34% and 27% for non-migrants.
claims.limitations: Loss shares refer to the latest disaster year reported by surveyed households, not annual expected losses.

claims.locator: PDF p.5, regional examples of resource competition and climate-related insecurity
claims.paraphrase: The report describes Mopti violence amid Fulani herder–Dogon farmer resource competition and links Gao drought-related yield loss with food insecurity and local conflict.
claims.limitations: Regional study uses prior literature and informant accounts; it does not isolate climate as a sufficient cause of conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It describes resource competition, drought-related yield loss and insecurity as interacting regional pressures.

claims.locator: PDF p.25, Gao climate-smart agriculture and Mali mediator-training passages
claims.paraphrase: Gao farmers reportedly use drip irrigation, crop rotation and drought-resistant crops; Mali informants described herder-farmer mediator training integrated with climate-smart agriculture.
claims.limitations: Study synthesizes informant reports and examples; it does not provide independent impact estimates for the Gao practices.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Mali informants explicitly connected herder-farmer mediator training with climate-smart agricultural initiatives.

claims.paraphrase: Across 20 priority communes (2018–24), WFP reports improved dietary diversity, fewer migration coping strategies and stronger cohesion; results varied regionally and were weaker for the poorest.
claims.limitations: WFP synopsis only; the full evaluation, named communes and subgroup estimates were not reviewed.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: WFP reports fewer negative coping strategies, including migration, and improved social cohesion.

claims.paraphrase: Asset and agricultural support strengthened resilience, but climate and security constrained effectiveness; community committees often lacked capacity and resources to maintain assets.
claims.limitations: Portal synopsis does not supply commune-level disaggregation or underlying evidence tables.

claims.locator: UNDP story, lines 27–40, Dembala testimony and water-point rehabilitation
claims.paraphrase: Dembala women described dry-season pump and well failures and fights over scarce water; rehabilitated potable-water points later restored drinking and irrigation access.
claims.limitations: Story does not evaluate impacts or locate Dembala's district.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: A resident linked water scarcity to water disputes.

claims.locator: UNDP story, lines 38–41, conflict/resource-grievance and gender/youth discussion
claims.paraphrase: UNDP says women travel farther for water and fuelwood and face heightened GBV risk in conflict zones; it also describes youth as vulnerable to extremist recruitment.
claims.limitations: Country-level programme narrative, not a representative estimate of GBV or recruitment.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links conflict-zone insecurity with GBV risk and climate-related youth recruitment vulnerability.

claims.locator: UNDP story, lines 47–51, Barahogon account of natural-resource rules
claims.paraphrase: A revitalized Dogon Barahogon institution reports forest-use rules regenerated trees and reduced resource conflict and flooding; Djenné and Mopti communities adopted its model.
claims.limitations: Account from the institution's president; no independent impact assessment.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Barahogon links earlier conflict and flooding with rain scarcity and forest loss.

access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.reuse_terms: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 stated in publication front matter.

search_audit.query: Mali Mopti Gao named communes climate drought flood vulnerability households local adaptation report
search_audit.outcome: Opened IIED household study for five named Mopti communes and UNDP Liptako-Gourma report for Mopti and Gao examples; IsDB contrasts broad northern and southern exposure zones. Site-level claims remain limited to reported evidence.

search_audit.query: Mali Liptako-Gourma Mopti Gao climate variability farmer herder conflict FCV mediators primary report
search_audit.outcome: Opened IsDB, IIED and UNDP report passages identifying resource/land competition, insecurity, climate-linked livelihood pressures and mobility; sources caution against a single climate-causes-conflict explanation.

search_audit.query: Mali insecurity conflict displacement restrict climate adaptation livelihoods service access drought
search_audit.outcome: Opened IsDB and IIED passages on violence limiting livelihood mobility, displacement and loss; WFP synopsis reports security constraints on programme effectiveness. No claim treats conflict as climate-driven.

search_audit.query: Mali community climate resilience local mediation adaptation performance evaluation communes
search_audit.outcome: Opened IsDB and UNDP evidence on household adaptations, climate-smart farming and local mediation, WFP's evaluation synopsis, and UNDP programme testimony on water access and traditional resource governance; program claims retain evaluation caveats.

gaps: The official Government of Mali page opened for the National Adaptation Plan reports technical/institutional validation of the 2026–2033 plan, but the plan document itself was not located and no implementation claim is made.
The full WFP Integrated Resilience Package evaluation PDF was not accessible through the public reader; claims are confined to its official synopsis and lack named-commune disaggregation.
The UNDP regional report states that insecurity restricted field access and may bias observations toward accessible areas; local conflict-climate findings are not causal estimates.
The sources reviewed do not establish national prevalence for the local Dembala and Barahogon examples or provide comparable, current subnational climate-conflict estimates.
